text: Only {deg:.0f}° (rescaled) of {sign} rises: Lilly "may not adventure judgment" when the first degrees ascend.
plain: The rising sign has only just begun ({deg:.0f}° of its 30): too early, by Lilly's rule.
basis: caution from horary, applied to elections (app)

text: {deg:.0f}° (rescaled) of {sign} rises: Lilly finds it "no wayes safe" when 27-29 degrees ascend.
plain: The rising sign has almost finished rising ({deg:.0f}° of its 30): too late, by Lilly's rule.
basis: caution from horary, applied to elections (app)

text: The Moon is in the Via Combusta (last half of Libra or first of Scorpio, rescaled).
plain: The Moon is on the unlucky "burnt road" (Via Combusta).

text: The Moon is void of course in {sign}: "All manner of matters goe hardly on".
plain: The Moon makes no further contact before leaving {sign}: things begun now tend to stall, so Lilly would wait.

text: Saturn is in the Ascendant: the matter "seldome or never comes to good".
plain: Saturn, the planet of delay, is rising.

text: {who} ({planet}) is combust. Lilly: "the combustion of any Planet is the greatest misfortune".
plain: {who_plain} ({planet}) is lost in the Sun's glare (combust), which Lilly counts among the most serious weaknesses: better to wait.
source: Lilly p.111; p.122 (Lord of the Ascendant combust)

text: {con} rises: no sign in Lilly, so there is no Lord of the Ascendant to elect by.
plain: {con} is rising, which has no sign in Lilly, so no planet stands for you.

text: The {h} cusp is in {con}, which has no sign in Lilly, so the matter has no lord; perfection cannot be read.
plain: The house of this matter (the {h}) begins in {con}, which has no sign in Lilly, so the matter has no planet.

text: {role}{planet}: net {net:+d} by Lilly's table (counted at half weight).
plain: {role_plain}{who_paren} is {word} (net {net:+d}).
basis: sourced scores; the 0.5 weight is an app choice

text: The lord of the {h} ({planet}) is retrograde: in Lilly a retrograde significator draws back from the matter (refrenation).
plain: {planet}, the planet of the matter, is moving backwards (retrograde): it draws back from the matter.

text: {planet} rules both the Ascendant and the {h}: one planet signifies both the person and the matter.
plain: One planet, {planet}, stands for both you and the matter, which binds the two together.

text: The Lord of the Ascendant ({a}) applies to a conjunction with the lord of the matter ({b}), {dev:.1f}° away: "brought to passe without any manner of let".
plain: {a}, the planet for you, is about to meet {b}, the planet of the matter: Lilly's clearest sign that the matter comes about.

text: {a} applies to {b} by conjunction, but both are cadent: perfected "with infinite losse of time, some difficulty, and much strugling".
plain: {a} is about to meet {b}, but both are in weak houses: it comes about slowly and with difficulty.

text: {a} applies to {b} by {asp} ({dev:.1f}° away), both dignified and out of good houses: "Things are also brought to a passe".
plain: {a} and {b} are moving into a friendly contact ({asp}), both well placed: things come about easily.

text: {a} applies to {b} by {asp} ({dev:.1f}° away), but not both dignified or not out of good houses.
plain: {a} and {b} are moving into a friendly contact ({asp}), but one is poorly placed: a weaker promise.

text: {a} applies to {b} by square ({dev:.1f}° away) and both have dignity: Lilly allows perfection by square "provided each Planet have dignity".
plain: {a} and {b} are moving into a tense contact (square), but both are strong: it can still come about, with effort.

text: {a} applies to {b} by square ({dev:.1f}° away) without dignity in both: Lilly says "otherwise not".
plain: {a} and {b} are moving into a tense contact (square) without the strength to carry it.

text: {a} applies to {b} by opposition ({dev:.1f}° away): Lilly "rarely" saw perfection this way, and "the Querent had been better the thing had been undone"; of marriages "the parties seldome agreed".
plain: {a} and {b} are moving into opposition: Lilly rarely saw things come about this way, and then with regret.

text: {a} and {b} are in mutual reception: "the thing is brought to passe".
plain: {a} and {b} each stand in the other's home ground: a sign of cooperation.

text: The Moon translates the light of {a} and {b} (separating from one, applying to the other).
plain: The Moon carries the light between {a} and {b}, like a go-between.
source: Lilly ch. XXI pp.124-126 (perfection) (translation of light)

text: The Moon applies by {asp} to {planet}, the natural significator. Compare Lilly on gathering a planet's herbs: the planet strong, "and the Moon in some manner in good aspect with him".
plain: The Moon is moving towards a friendly contact ({asp}) with {planet}, the natural planet of this matter.
source: Lilly p.65 (Jupiter), and likewise in the other planet chapters

text: The Moon applies by {asp} to the fortune {planet}.
plain: The Moon is moving towards a friendly contact ({asp}) with {planet}, a helpful planet.

text: The Moon applies by {asp} to the infortune {planet}.
plain: The Moon is moving towards a hard contact ({asp}) with {planet}, one of the difficult planets.

text: It is the planetary hour of {planet}, the natural significator.
plain: It is the planetary hour of {planet}, the natural planet of this matter.
source: Lilly p.61, p.65 (each planet rules its day and hours)
basis: sourced hours; the use in elections is an app rule

text: It is the planetary hour of {planet}, an infortune.
plain: It is the planetary hour of {planet}, one of the difficult planets.
